title: Completion failures and launcher lifetime
intro: Required corrections to the incumbent launcher's four known failure gaps, with its agreed one-session CLI lifetime. Current-source views and the unselected regrouping remain context. Boxes denote in-process responsibilities, not packages or deployment containers. Graph views start at the dark Start here node; sequences start at their first message. The A0–A15 inventory remains the source observation. Design and rendering establish no runtime conformance.

discussion.title: Retain failure facts through cleanup, then exit the launcher
discussion.status: Repair design; implementation and runtime checks pending
discussion.summary: Consumed cancellation must survive a no-ending error. Worker teardown gates admission, partial allocators report checked cleanup, and failed exec retains the terminal lease and spawn cause. The one-session CLI owns signal/terminal authority until settlement and exit; a persistent runner has a separate contract. Corrections preserve the incumbent and do not select a package, comparative target or migration.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Added the required error-carried cancellation and original-failure/cleanup/result precedence, including no-ending settlement.

diagrams.title: Required failure facts and settlement precedence
diagrams.caption: Required repair contract, not current implementation or observed conformance. Solid arrows are decisions and outcome order. Retained runner cancellation can come from success or error; worker reap and allocator cleanup reports belong to their own resource owners. An original missing/invalid-result failure is checked before cleanup precedence. Every operational report remains available even when cancellation wins. See the completion specification and discriminating evidence matrix.

diagrams.title: Owned terminal handoff followed by failed exec
diagrams.caption: Proposed bounded correction for an interactive lease initially owned by the launcher. Checked handback requires no competing foreground transfer or unrelated reuse of the recorded group identity through recovery; CLI lifetime alone does not establish those premises. The record never authorises post-reap group signalling. All recovery errors stay beside the original spawn errno. Started means spawn-reported success, not confirmed exec. Background launches take no lease. Pinned Rust source and this diagram establish no PTY conformance; real checks remain owed.

diagrams.title: One-session launcher owns entry through final exit
diagrams.caption: The human agreed the first native consumer's process lifetime. Solid arrows show required lifetime order; the dotted edge names the separate persistent-runner contract. Child entry transparency remains distinct from returning-host restoration. The CLI still owes checked launch cleanup and late cancellation joining. No native package, independent adopting project or runtime result is established by this design.
